transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I suppose I’m here because I’ve been feeling a bit stuck. Not in a dramatic way, really, but there’s this quiet feeling I can’t seem to shake that maybe the best part of my life is behind me. And I keep thinking that even if I plan better or try to be disciplined, I’m not sure I can get back to feeling like myself. I don’t know if that makes sense.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I guess it’s been… a little over three years now. It started after I had a hiking injury, and it’s just sort of stayed with me since then. About three years and three months, if I’m counting right. Is that the kind of timeframe you mean?
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like before this feeling started?

I’m not completely sure how to answer that. I mean, I still do some of the things I used to enjoy, and sometimes they’re… fine. Maybe not quite the same, but I wouldn’t want to overstate it. I suppose I’ve noticed things don’t always feel as satisfying as they used to, but I can’t say if that’s what you mean.
Do you still find pleasure in the things you're doing, even if it's not as satisfying as before?

I think I do, yes… at least some of the time. It’s not as easy or as full as it used to be, maybe, but I wouldn’t say there’s no pleasure at all. If I’m with family or doing something familiar, there can still be nice moments. I guess it just doesn’t always stay with me the same way. Is that answering what you’re asking?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since you started feeling this way?
Not really, no. I mean, my weight’s gone up and down a little like it does, but I haven’t noticed anything I’d call significant. I haven’t been tracking it closely, though—should I be?
Have you ever had thoughts of wanting to harm yourself or end your life since you started feeling this way?
I… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve felt low, but not like I wanted to hurt myself or end my life. At least, that’s not something I’ve been thinking about. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Are there things that you used to find pleasurable but no longer enjoy at all?

I don’t think there’s anything I no longer enjoy at all. Some things feel a bit flatter than they used to, maybe, but if I actually do them, I can usually get something out of them. So… no, not completely gone, I’d say. Does that make sense?
Have you experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt significantly depressed most of the day?

Yes… I think so. I wouldn’t say I’m crying all day or anything dramatic like that, but there have definitely been stretches where most days there’s this low, gray feeling underneath everything. Even if I’m in the studio or having dinner with my wife, it’s sort of still there in the background. Does that count as “significantly depressed”?
Are there any activities that you used to find pleasurable but now feel completely neutral or unenjoyable to you?

Not completely neutral, no. I mean, I may not get as much out of things as I used to, but I wouldn’t say there’s anything I used to enjoy that now feels like nothing at all. Maybe I’m splitting hairs, but… I don’t think so.
Have you experienced more than two of these periods of significant depression in the past three years?

More than two… I think, yes, if I’m being honest. It’s not like I can always mark a clean beginning and end, but over the last few years there have been several stretches where most days had that low, gray feeling underneath everything. Not dramatic, not me falling apart, but there even when I’m in the studio or at dinner with my wife. So… yes, I suppose that would count?
Are there things that used to bring you joy but now feel completely uninteresting to you?

I don’t think I’d say completely uninteresting, no. Some things feel a little flatter than they used to, maybe, but I still can get something out of them. So… I don’t want to overstate it. I wouldn’t say they bring me no joy at all.
Are there things that you used to enjoy that now bring you no pleasure at all?

No, I don’t think so. I know I’ve said some things feel a bit muted, maybe not as satisfying as they once were, but “no pleasure at all” sounds stronger than what I mean. I still enjoy things, at least some. Does that make sense?
Are there any activities that you once found pleasurable but now find you are unable to enjoy at all?

I don’t think I’d put it that strongly, no. There may be times when I don’t feel as much from things as I’d like, but I can’t really think of something I used to enjoy that I’m now unable to enjoy at all. I hope that’s answering what you mean.
Are there any activities that you once found pleasurable but now bring you significantly less pleasure than they used to?

I’m not sure I’d say “significantly,” no. I mean, some things maybe don’t feel quite as bright as they used to, but I haven’t really noticed a big drop in pleasure from any particular activity. I still get some enjoyment out of things. I hope that’s the kind of distinction you’re asking about.
Are there things that you used to enjoy that now feel like a chore to do?

Maybe a little, yes. I still do the things—I get up, do the shopping, tinker with projects and all that—but sometimes the setup around them feels heavier than it should. Even getting ready for a mentoring session, or walking around at a community event, can leave me pretty worn out afterward. Not in a dramatic way, I guess, but enough that a nap doesn’t really fix it. Does that answer what you mean by “chore”?
Are there things that you used to enjoy that now bring you little to no pleasure?

No, I don’t think so—not little to no pleasure. Some things take more effort than I’d like, or I may not feel quite as enthusiastic beforehand, but once I’m doing them I can still get something out of them. I wouldn’t want to overstate it. Does that make sense?
Are there things that you used to enjoy that now feel completely empty or joyless to you?

Completely empty or joyless? No, I don’t think I’d put it that strongly. I mean, I have off days where something feels a bit flat, or I’m slower to get into it, but not like it’s totally gone or hollow. I can still find some pleasure in things once I’m there. Is that clear enough?
Are there things that bring you little to no pleasure when you're doing them?

I don’t think so, not really. There might be moments where I’m distracted or it takes me a while to settle into something, but while I’m actually doing it, I can usually find at least some enjoyment in it. I wouldn’t say there are things that bring me little to no pleasure. Is that answering it the way you mean?
Have you been experiencing feelings of worthlessness or guilt that have persisted over time?

I don’t think so, not in any persistent way. I mean, I can second-guess myself or feel I could’ve handled something better, like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been carrying around strong feelings of worthlessness or guilt over time. Does that answer what you’re asking?
